records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, μετῆρεν ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.
records.gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus the words these, he moved away from the Galilee and came into the regions of the Judea beyond the Jordan.
pieces: When Jesus had finished saying these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left Galilee and went on into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

L.1: And it happened, when Jesus had finished these words, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved on from Galilee and came into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

R.1: When Jesus finished saying these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left Galilee. He went south to the land of Judea and to the area on the east side of the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished these words: the formula that closes the fourth long speech
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech with these words (7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 26:1). This one closes the teaching of chapter 18.

decisions.choice: the region of Judea beyond the Jordan: Judea, and the land east of the river through which Jesus traveled to reach it
alternatives: a part of Judea lying east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Judea itself lay west of the Jordan. The phrase most likely joins the two areas Jesus now works in; Mark 10:1 says "Judea and beyond the Jordan". Travelers from Galilee often went south on the east side of the river.

decisions.choice: went south to the land of Judea and to the area on the east side of the Jordan River
alternatives: came into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan
decisions.reason: Readable names both areas and says where they lie.

records.heading: Jesus leaves Galilee for Judea

records.source: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς ἐκεῖ.
records.gloss: And followed him crowds many, and he healed them there.
pieces: Great crowds went after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

L.2: And large crowds followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them there.

R.2: Large crowds of people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed the sick people there.

decisions.choice: he healed them: he healed the sick among the crowds
alternatives: every person in the crowds was ill
decisions.reason: As in 12:15 and 15:30, "them" means those in the crowds who needed healing.

decisions.choice: the sick people
decisions.reason: Readable says whom Jesus healed.

records.source: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Φαρισαῖοι πειράζοντες αὐτὸν καὶ λέγοντες· Εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνθρώπῳ ἀπολῦσαι τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ κατὰ πᾶσαν αἰτίαν;
records.gloss: And came to him Pharisees testing him and saying, If it is lawful for a man to divorce the wife of him for every cause?
pieces: Some Pharisees came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the test. "Does the law allow a man to divorce his wife for any reason at all?" they asked.

L.3: And Pharisees came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and saying, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?"

R.3: Some Pharisees came to Jesus. They wanted to trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with a hard question. So they asked, "Does God's law let a man divorce his wife for any reason he wants?"

decisions.choice: testing him: trying to catch him out
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the Pharisees in 16:1 and 22:35. Any answer would set Jesus against one party or another.

decisions.choice: for any cause: the debate over the grounds for divorce in Deuteronomy 24:1
alternatives: a general question whether divorce is ever right
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a husband finding "something indecent" in his wife. Jewish teachers disagreed about what that meant: the school of Shammai allowed divorce only for unfaithfulness, the school of Hillel for almost any cause (Mishnah Gittin 9:10). See 5:31-32.

decisions.choice: a man divorcing his wife: in Jewish law only the husband could divorce
decisions.reason: As at 5:31, the question is put from the husband's side, because only he had the right to end the marriage.

decisions.choice: the test may also have had a political edge
alternatives: a question about the law only
decisions.reason: Jesus was now in the territory of Herod Antipas, who had put John the Baptist in prison for condemning his marriage (14:3-4). Matthew does not say this was part of the trap.

decisions.choice: Does the law allow (B); Does God's law let (R)
decisions.reason: "Lawful" means allowed by the law of Moses; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.heading: A question about divorce

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι ὁ κτίσας ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν· Ἕνεκα τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ κολληθήσεται τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν;
records.gloss: He but answering said, Not did you read that the [one] having created from beginning male and female made them \v 5 and said, On account of this will leave a man the father and the mother and will be joined to the wife of him, and will be the two into flesh one?
pieces: Jesus answered, "Have you never read that the Creator, at the beginning, made them male and female?
And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'That is why a man will leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh.'

L.4: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "Have you not read that the one who created [them] from [the] beginning made them male and female,
L.5: and said, 'For this reason a man will leave [his] father and mother and will be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh'?

R.4: Jesus answered, "Have you not read in the Scriptures what God did in the beginning? He made people male and female.
R.5: And God said, 'That is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife. The two of them will become one, as if they were one body.'

decisions.choice: male and female he made them: Genesis 1:27
decisions.reason: Jesus goes behind the law of divorce to creation. God made humankind male and female from the first, and marriage belongs to that purpose.

decisions.choice: Genesis 2:24, quoted as the Greek translation of Genesis has it
decisions.reason: "The two" is in the Greek translation of Genesis but not in the Hebrew text, which says "they will become one flesh". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: and said: the Creator is the speaker of Genesis 2:24
decisions.reason: In Genesis the words are the narrator's comment. Jesus treats them as what God himself said, so they carry God's authority.

decisions.choice: the one who created, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the one who made, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have the more common verb "made". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with "he said" for the Creator
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long question in two so the quotation is clear.

decisions.choice: will become one, as if they were one body
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of one flesh.

records.source: ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ σὰρξ μία.
records.gloss: So that no longer are they two but flesh one.
pieces: So they are not two any longer; they are one flesh.

L.6: So they are no longer two, but one flesh.

R.6: So a husband and wife are no longer two people. They are one.

decisions.choice: one flesh: one life and one household, joined in body and in every part of life
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means the whole person. Husband and wife become a new unit, as close as one body, which is why Jesus goes on to forbid parting them.

decisions.choice: a husband and wife
decisions.reason: Readable says who "they" are.

records.source: ὃ οὖν ὁ θεὸς συνέζευξεν ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω.
records.gloss: What therefore the God joined together, a man not let separate.
pieces: What God has yoked together, then, no human being may pull apart."

L.6: Therefore what God has joined together, let {{gender:a human being|man}} not separate."

R.6: God has joined them together. So no one should separate them."

decisions.choice: joined together: yoked together, as a pair
decisions.reason: The verb pictures two animals under one yoke. God is the one who joins husband and wife.

decisions.choice: let not a human being separate: a command, aimed first at the husband who would divorce
alternatives: a statement that divorce is impossible
decisions.reason: "Human being" stands against "God". The verb forbids people to undo what God has done; it does not say that a marriage cannot be broken.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a human being|man}}
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, set against God, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: yoked together
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in the verb.

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Τί οὖν Μωϋσῆς ἐνετείλατο δοῦναι βιβλίον ἀποστασίου καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν;
records.gloss: They say to him, Why then Moses commanded to give a scroll of divorce and to divorce her?
pieces: They said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Then why did Moses order a man to give his wife a written notice of divorce and send her away?"

L.7: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why then did Moses command [a man] to give [her] a certificate of divorce and to divorce her?"

R.7: The Pharisees said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Then why did Moses give us a law about divorce? He said a man must give his wife a paper saying that she is divorced, and then he can send her away."

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 24:1-4: the written notice of divorce
alternatives: a command that men must divorce
decisions.reason: The law did not command divorce. It assumed that divorce happened and required the husband to give his wife a written notice, which left her free to marry again (see 5:31).

decisions.choice: commanded: the Pharisees' word, which Jesus corrects to "allowed" in 19:8
alternatives: a fair summary of the law
decisions.reason: The question makes Moses' rule sound like an order. Jesus answers that Moses only permitted divorce.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: written notice of divorce (B); a paper saying that she is divorced (R)
decisions.reason: As at 5:31.

records.source: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Μωϋσῆς πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἐπέτρεψεν ὑμῖν ἀπολῦσαι τὰς γυναῖκας ὑμῶν, ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς δὲ οὐ γέγονεν οὕτως.
records.gloss: He says to them, Moses in view of the hardness of heart of you allowed you to divorce the wives of you, from beginning but not it has been thus.
pieces: Jesus answered, "It was because your hearts were so hard that Moses permitted you to divorce your wives. That is not how things were at the beginning.

L.8: He says to them, "Because of your hardness of heart Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but from [the] beginning it has not been so.

R.8: Jesus said to them, "Moses let you divorce your wives because you were so stubborn. But that is not what God planned when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} first made people.

decisions.choice: hardness of heart: a stubborn refusal to do God's will
alternatives: hard feelings between husband and wife
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls the prophets' charge against Israel (Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4). The rule about divorce allowed for human sin; it did not show what God wants.

decisions.choice: your: Jesus includes his hearers with Israel in Moses' day
decisions.reason: The same hardness that made the law necessary is still present in those who ask.

decisions.choice: from the beginning it has not been so: God's purpose at creation never included divorce
alternatives: divorce did not exist until Moses
decisions.reason: The perfect tense looks at the state of things as God made them and as they still should be. Jesus appeals to creation (19:4-6) over the later rule.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: that is not what God planned when he first made people
alternatives: from the beginning it has not been so
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the beginning" refers to.

records.source: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐπὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσας μοιχᾶται.
records.gloss: I say but to you that whoever divorces the wife of him not for sexual immorality and marries another commits adultery, and the [one] a divorced [woman] having married commits adultery.
pieces: And I tell you this: a man who divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual unfaithfulness and then marries someone else commits adultery, and the man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."

L.9: But I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."

R.9: But I tell you, if a man divorces his wife for any reason except sexual unfaithfulness, and then he marries another woman, he is guilty of adultery. And a man who marries a divorced woman is guilty of adultery too."

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual unfaithfulness by the wife
decisions.reason: As at 5:32, the word covers sexual sin of many kinds, and in a saying about marriage it most likely means the wife's unfaithfulness. Others limit it to marriages the law forbade (Leviticus 18) or to unfaithfulness during betrothal (as in 1:19).

decisions.choice: the wording of the SBLGNT, with the closing words about marrying a divorced woman
alternatives: except on account of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery, as in 5:32, the reading of some manuscripts
the closing words are missing in a number of early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts give the exception in the words of 5:32 and say the husband "makes her commit adultery". Several early manuscripts lack the final clause, which may have been added from 5:32. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the exception applies to the whole case: divorce and remarriage
alternatives: the exception permits divorce but not remarriage
decisions.reason: The exception stands between "divorces" and "marries another", and most naturally governs both. Some read it as allowing a husband to separate from an unfaithful wife but not to marry again.

decisions.choice: I tell you: Jesus speaks on his own authority beside Moses
decisions.reason: As in the sayings of 5:21-48, Jesus sets his own word beside what the law allowed.

records.source: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Εἰ οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ αἰτία τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μετὰ τῆς γυναικός, οὐ συμφέρει γαμῆσαι.
records.gloss: Say to him the disciples, If thus is the case of the man with the wife, not it is better to marry.
pieces: His disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If that is how it stands between a man and his wife, then it would be better not to marry at all."

L.10: The disciples say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If such is the case of the man with [his] wife, it is not better to marry."

R.10: Jesus's followers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If a man cannot divorce his wife, it is better for him not to get married."

decisions.choice: case: the situation, the terms on which a man is bound to his wife
decisions.reason: It is the same word as "cause" in 19:3. The Pharisees asked about a cause for divorce; the disciples now speak of the "case" of marriage itself.

decisions.choice: it is not better to marry: marriage seems too great a risk if it cannot be ended
decisions.reason: The disciples are taken aback by how strict Jesus is. Their remark leads to his words about those who do not marry.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: if a man cannot divorce his wife
alternatives: if such is the case of the man with his wife
decisions.reason: Readable says what "such" refers to.

records.heading: Those who do not marry

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ πάντες χωροῦσι τὸν λόγον τοῦτον ἀλλ’ οἷς δέδοται.
records.gloss: He but said to them, Not all accept the word this but [those] to whom it has been given.
pieces: He answered them, "This saying is not something everyone can accept. Only those to whom it has been given can do so.

L.11: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Not all [people] accept this word, but [only those] to whom it has been given.

R.11: Jesus said to them, "Not everyone can accept this teaching. Only the people God gives this gift to can accept it.

decisions.choice: this word: the disciples' saying that it is better not to marry
alternatives: Jesus's own teaching on divorce in 19:9
decisions.reason: What follows is about those who do not marry, so "this word" most likely points to the disciples' remark: not everyone can live unmarried. Others take it as Jesus's teaching on divorce, which only those given grace can keep.

decisions.choice: to whom it has been given: God gives the ability
decisions.reason: The passive points to God as the giver, as in 13:11.

decisions.choice: accept: make room for, take in and live by
decisions.reason: The verb means to have room for something. Here it means to receive a teaching and be able to live it.

decisions.choice: the people God gives this gift to
alternatives: those to whom it has been given
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver.

records.source: εἰσὶν γὰρ εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ἐγεννήθησαν οὕτως, καὶ εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες εὐνουχίσθησαν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες εὐνούχισαν ἑαυτοὺς διὰ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
records.gloss: There are for eunuchs who from womb of mother were born thus, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by the men, and there are eunuchs who made eunuchs themselves for the sake of the kingdom of the heavens.
pieces: For some are eunuchs because they were born that way; some have been made eunuchs by others; and some have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.

L.12: For there are eunuchs who were born so from [their] mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by {{gender:people|men}}, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of the heavens.

R.12: Some men are eunuchs: they cannot marry and have children. Some were born that way. Others were made that way by other people, who cut their bodies. And some choose to live like eunuchs and not marry, for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: men unable to father children, either from birth or by castration
decisions.reason: In the ancient world some men were castrated to serve in royal households (Acts 8:27). The law kept such men from the assembly (Deuteronomy 23:1), but God promised them a place among his people (Isaiah 56:3-5).

decisions.choice: made themselves eunuchs: chose not to marry
decisions.reason: The third kind is a picture. Jesus speaks of people who freely give up marriage, as the first two kinds could not marry. The law forbade cutting the body in this way (Deuteronomy 23:1), and Jesus does not command it.

decisions.choice: for the sake of the kingdom of heaven: to be free to serve God's kingdom
alternatives: in order to enter the kingdom
because they have been divorced and do not remarry
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means giving up marriage to give oneself to the work of the kingdom, as Paul says in 1 Corinthians 7:32-35. Some take it as the way a divorced disciple stays single (19:9), or as a condition for entering the kingdom.

decisions.choice: they cannot marry and have children; who cut their bodies; choose to live like eunuchs and not marry
alternatives: eunuchs; made eunuchs; made themselves eunuchs
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a eunuch is and what the third kind means.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

records.source: ὁ δυνάμενος χωρεῖν χωρείτω.
records.gloss: The [one] being able to accept, let him accept.
pieces: Let anyone who is able to accept this accept it."

L.12: The one who is able to accept [this], let {{gender:them|him}} accept [it]."

R.12: If you are able to accept this teaching, then accept it."

decisions.choice: let him accept it: an invitation to those given the gift, not a command for all
alternatives: a rule that all disciples must stay unmarried
decisions.reason: The saying echoes 19:11. Remaining unmarried is for those able to receive it, as "whoever has ears" in 11:15.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The saying is for anyone able to accept it.

decisions.choice: If you are able ... then accept it
alternatives: The one who is able, let him accept
decisions.reason: Readable speaks directly to the hearer.

records.source: Τότε προσηνέχθησαν αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιθῇ αὐτοῖς καὶ προσεύξηται· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: Then were brought to him little children that the hands he might lay on them and might pray; the but disciples rebuked them.
pieces: After this, some people brought young children to Jesus so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on them and pray for them. But the disciples spoke sternly to the people.

L.13: Then little children were brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might lay [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on them and pray; but the disciples rebuked them.

R.13: Then some people brought their little children to Jesus. They wanted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on the children and pray for them. But Jesus's followers told the people to stop.

decisions.choice: to lay hands on them and pray: to bless them
decisions.reason: Laying hands on someone with prayer was a way of blessing (Genesis 48:14). Parents wanted a blessing from a holy man for their children.

decisions.choice: rebuked them: those who brought the children
decisions.reason: "Them" most naturally means the people bringing the children, though it could include the children too. The disciples thought they were a bother.

decisions.choice: little children: young children
decisions.reason: The word is used of young children, as in 18:2-5.

decisions.choice: some people brought
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who brought them; the Greek is passive.

records.heading: Jesus blesses the children

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτὰ ἐλθεῖν πρός με, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
records.gloss: The but Jesus said, Let the little children and not forbid them to come to me, of the for such is the kingdom of the heavens.
pieces: Jesus said, "Let the children be. Do not prevent them from coming to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because the kingdom of heaven is for those who are like them."

L.14: But Jesus said, "Let the little children [be], and do not forbid them to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for the kingdom of the heavens belongs to such [as these]."

R.14: But Jesus said, "Let the little children come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Do not stop them! The kingdom of heaven belongs to people who are like these children."

decisions.choice: of such is the kingdom: it belongs to children and to those who are like them
alternatives: it is made up of children
decisions.reason: "Such" means people of this kind. As in 18:3-4, the kingdom is received by those who, like children, are lowly and depend on others.

decisions.choice: let: leave them alone, allow them
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to forgive, to leave or to allow; here it means to let the children be.

records.source: καὶ ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἐπορεύθη ἐκεῖθεν.
records.gloss: And having laid the hands on them he went from there.
pieces: He put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on them, and then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on from there.

L.15: And after laying [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on from there.

R.15: Jesus put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on the children to bless them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place.

decisions.choice: laying his hands on them: Jesus did what the parents asked
alternatives: a different act from the blessing asked for
decisions.reason: Matthew says simply that Jesus gave them the blessing the disciples had tried to prevent.

decisions.choice: to bless them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the laying on of hands meant (19:13).

records.source: Καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς προσελθὼν αὐτῷ εἶπεν· Διδάσκαλε, τί ἀγαθὸν ποιήσω ἵνα σχῶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον;
records.gloss: And behold, one having come to him said, Teacher, what good shall I do that I may have life eternal?
pieces: Then a man came up to Jesus and asked, "Teacher, what good thing must I do to gain eternal life?"

L.16: And look, someone came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Teacher, what good [thing] must I do so that I may have eternal life?"

R.16: One day a man came to Jesus and asked, "Teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?"

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come, life with God that does not end
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:2 speaks of those who will rise "to everlasting life". In 19:17 the same life is called simply "life", and in 19:23-24 entering it is entering the kingdom.

decisions.choice: what good thing must I do: he thinks of a deed that will earn life
decisions.reason: He asks what single good act is needed. Jesus's answer turns him from good deeds to the one who is good.

decisions.choice: Teacher, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Good Teacher, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "Good Teacher", as in Mark 10:17 and Luke 18:18. See the note on 19:17. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); then (B); one day (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: a man
decisions.reason: Matthew says only "one"; he is later called a young man (19:20) and rich (19:22).

records.heading: A young man asks about eternal life

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με ἐρωτᾷς περὶ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ;
records.gloss: He but said to him, Why me do you ask about the good?
pieces: Jesus answered him, "Why ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about what is good?

L.17: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Why do you ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about what is good?

R.17: Jesus said to him, "Why are you asking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} what is good?

decisions.choice: Why do you ask me about what is good? the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Why do you call me good? the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts of Matthew have this wording. Many later manuscripts read "Why do you call me good?", with "Good Teacher" in 19:16, as in Mark 10:17-18 and Luke 18:18-19, most likely made to agree with those Gospels. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: what is good: goodness is defined by God, not by a deed of one's choosing
alternatives: Jesus refuses to talk about goodness
decisions.reason: Jesus turns the man's question about a good deed toward God, who alone is good and who has already said what is good in his commands (Micah 6:8).

records.source: εἷς ἐστιν ὁ ἀγαθός· εἰ δὲ θέλεις εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν, τήρησον τὰς ἐντολάς.
records.gloss: One is the good; if but you want into the life to enter, keep the commandments.
pieces: There is one who is good. If you wish to enter into life, obey the commandments."

L.17: One is the good [one]; but if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments."

R.17: Only God is good. If you want to have eternal life, obey God's commands."

decisions.choice: one is good: God
decisions.reason: Mark 10:18 and Luke 18:19 say "no one is good except God alone". The "one" recalls the confession that the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4).

decisions.choice: enter into life: receive eternal life (19:16)
decisions.reason: As in 18:8-9, "life" stands for the life of the age to come.

decisions.choice: One is good, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: No one is good except one, God, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts give the wording of Mark 10:18 here; see the note on 19:17. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Only God is good; have eternal life
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says which life is meant (19:16).

records.source: λέγει αὐτῷ· Ποίας;
records.gloss: He says to him, Which?
pieces: "Which ones?" the man asked.

decisions.choice: which ones: which of the commands matter for this
decisions.reason: The word can mean "what sort". The man may be asking which commands count most, a question teachers debated (22:36).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear who is speaking.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τὸ Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐ ψευδομαρτυρήσεις, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καὶ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
records.gloss: The but Jesus said, The You will not murder, You will not commit adultery, You will not steal, You will not bear false witness, \v 19 Honor the father and the mother, and You will love the neighbor of you as yourself.
pieces: Jesus said, "'Do not commit murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not give false testimony;
honor your father and your mother'; and 'love your neighbor as yourself.'"

L.18: And Jesus said, "'You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness;
L.19: honor [your] father and mother'; and 'you shall love your neighbor as yourself.'"

R.18: Jesus answered, "'Do not murder anyone. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about other people.
R.19: Honor your father and mother.' And, 'Love other people as much as you love yourself.'"

decisions.choice: the commandments of the second table: Exodus 20:12-16; Deuteronomy 5:16-20
alternatives: a new list of Jesus's own
decisions.reason: Jesus names the sixth to ninth commandments and then the fifth. All of them concern how one treats other people.

decisions.choice: love your neighbor as yourself: Leviticus 19:18
decisions.reason: Only Matthew adds this command here. It sums up the others, and Jesus calls it the second great commandment (22:39).

decisions.choice: the: the article marks what follows as a quotation
alternatives: a word with its own meaning
decisions.reason: The Greek article introduces the list, like quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Do not commit murder; Do not commit adultery (B); Do not murder anyone (R)
decisions.reason: As at 5:21 and 5:27, Balanced and Readable give the commands in the plain form of a command.

decisions.choice: Do not tell lies about other people
decisions.reason: Readable says what false witness is.

records.source: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ νεανίσκος· Πάντα ταῦτα ἐφύλαξα· τί ἔτι ὑστερῶ;
records.gloss: Says to him the young man, All these I have kept; what still do I lack?
pieces: The young man said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I have obeyed every one of these. What am I still missing?"

L.20: The young man says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All these I have kept; what do I still lack?"

R.20: The young man said, "I have obeyed all these commands. What else do I need to do?"

decisions.choice: young man: a man in the prime of life
decisions.reason: The word was used of men from youth to about forty. Only Matthew calls him young.

decisions.choice: what do I still lack: he senses that something is missing
alternatives: a boast that nothing is lacking
decisions.reason: He has kept the commands, yet he asks what more is needed. Jesus answers that question in 19:21.

decisions.choice: I have kept, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: I have kept from my youth, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "from my youth", as in Mark 10:20 and Luke 18:21. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰ θέλεις τέλειος εἶναι, ὕπαγε πώλησόν σου τὰ ὑπάρχοντα καὶ δὸς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
records.gloss: Said to him the Jesus, If you want perfect to be, go sell of you the possessions and give to poor, and you will have treasure in heavens, and come follow me.
pieces: Jesus told him, "Do you want to be perfect? Then go, sell your property, and give the money to people who are poor, and treasure in heaven will be yours. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.21: Jesus said to him, "If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give [them] to [the] poor, and you will have treasure in [the] heavens; and come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.21: Jesus told him, "If you want to be perfect, go and sell everything you own. Give the money to poor people. Then you will have riches in heaven. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: perfect: complete, whole, lacking nothing
decisions.reason: This is the word of 5:48. It answers the man's question "what do I still lack?". Being whole means giving God undivided love, here shown by giving up wealth to follow Jesus. It does not set up a second, higher level of disciple.

decisions.choice: treasure in heaven: what God keeps for those who give and obey
alternatives: a reward earned by good deeds
decisions.reason: As in 6:19-21, what is given away for God is kept by God.

decisions.choice: come, follow me: the call to be a disciple
alternatives: a request to walk with Jesus that day
decisions.reason: These are the words Jesus used to call the fishermen and Matthew (4:19; 9:9). The way to life is to follow Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: riches
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word.

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ νεανίσκος τὸν λόγον ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος, ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.
records.gloss: Having heard but the young man the word he went away grieving, he was for having possessions many.
pieces: When the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he owned a great deal of property.

L.22: But when the young man heard this word, he went away grieving, for he had many possessions.

R.22: When the young man heard this, he was very sad, and he went away. He was very rich.

decisions.choice: grieving: sad and troubled
decisions.reason: The verb means to be sorrowful. He wants eternal life but will not let go of his wealth.

decisions.choice: possessions: property, likely land and goods
decisions.reason: The word is used of property, especially fields and estates (as in Acts 5:1).

decisions.choice: He was very rich
decisions.reason: Readable states the point simply.

records.source: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πλούσιος δυσκόλως εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν·
records.gloss: The and Jesus said to the disciples of him, Truly I say to you that a rich [man] with difficulty will enter into the kingdom of the heavens;
pieces: Then Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Truly I tell you, a rich person will find it hard to get into the kingdom of heaven.

L.23: And Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Truly I tell you that a rich [{{gender:person|man}}] will enter the kingdom of the heavens with difficulty;

R.23: Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "I tell you the truth, it is hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.

decisions.choice: with difficulty: hardly, only with great trouble
decisions.reason: The word means hard to do. The next saying (19:24) shows how hard.

decisions.choice: a rich person: wealth holds people back from following Jesus
decisions.reason: As the young man just showed, wealth can hold a heart so firmly that a person will not give it up for God (6:24).

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: a rich [{{gender:person|man}}]
decisions.reason: The saying is about any rich person.

records.heading: Hard for the rich

records.source: πάλιν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρυπήματος ῥαφίδος εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Again and I say to you, easier it is a camel through eye of a needle to go than a rich [man] into the kingdom of the God.
pieces: I say it again: a camel could pass through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could enter the kingdom of God."

L.24: And again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than [for] a rich [{{gender:person|man}}] [to enter] into the kingdom of God."

R.24: I will say it again. It would be easier for a camel to go through the hole in a sewing needle than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom."

decisions.choice: a camel through the eye of a needle: something impossible
decisions.reason: The camel was the largest animal in the land and the eye of a needle the smallest opening. The picture is meant to be absurd, like the camel swallowed in 23:24. The disciples' question and Jesus's answer (19:25-26) show that it is impossible for people.

decisions.choice: a real camel and a real sewing needle
alternatives: a narrow gate in Jerusalem called the Needle's Eye
a rope, by a change of one letter
decisions.reason: The story of a small gate called the Needle's Eye is told only centuries later, and there is no evidence for such a gate in Jesus's day. The reading "rope" is found only in a few late manuscripts. Both try to soften a saying meant to shock.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: the same as the kingdom of heaven in 19:23
decisions.reason: Matthew usually says "kingdom of heaven" but sometimes "kingdom of God" (12:28; 21:31, 43). The two sayings stand side by side here.

decisions.choice: a rich [{{gender:person|man}}]
decisions.reason: As in 19:23.

decisions.choice: the hole in a sewing needle
decisions.reason: Readable says what the eye of a needle is.

records.source: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο σφόδρα λέγοντες· Τίς ἄρα δύναται σωθῆναι;
records.gloss: Having heard and the disciples were astonished greatly saying, Who then is able to be saved?
pieces: The disciples were utterly amazed at this. "Then who can be saved?" they asked.

L.25: And when the disciples heard [this], they were greatly astonished, saying, "Who then can be saved?"

R.25: When Jesus's followers heard this, they were very surprised. They asked, "Then who can be saved?"

decisions.choice: greatly astonished: wealth was widely seen as a sign of God's blessing
alternatives: surprised that rich people were mentioned
decisions.reason: The law promised plenty to those who obey (Deuteronomy 28:1-14). If even the rich, who seemed blessed, cannot enter, the disciples ask who can.

decisions.choice: be saved: be rescued for the life of the age to come
alternatives: be kept safe in this life
decisions.reason: In this passage being saved means having eternal life (19:16) and entering the kingdom (19:24).

decisions.choice: were astonished: the imperfect tense, they kept on being amazed
decisions.reason: The tense pictures continuing amazement.

records.source: ἐμβλέψας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις τοῦτο ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν, παρὰ δὲ θεῷ πάντα δυνατά.
records.gloss: Having looked at [them] and the Jesus said to them, With men this impossible is, with but God all things possible.
pieces: Jesus looked straight at them and said, "For human beings this cannot be done, but for God everything is possible."

L.26: And Jesus looked at [them] and said to them, "With {{gender:human beings|men}} this is impossible, but with God all things [are] possible."

R.26: Jesus looked at them and said, "People cannot save themselves. But God can do anything."

decisions.choice: this: being saved
alternatives: a camel going through a needle
decisions.reason: "This" refers to the disciples' question. No one, rich or poor, can bring about salvation by human power.

decisions.choice: with God all things are possible: the words to Abraham and Sarah
decisions.reason: God asked, "Is anything too hard for the LORD?" when he promised Sarah a son (Genesis 18:14). Job confesses that God can do all things (Job 42:2).

decisions.choice: looked at them: looked intently
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a steady, searching look.

decisions.choice: {{gender:human beings|men}}
decisions.reason: As in 9:8, the word means human beings.

decisions.choice: People cannot save themselves
decisions.reason: Readable says what is impossible.

records.source: Τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι· τί ἄρα ἔσται ἡμῖν;
records.gloss: Then answering the Peter said to him, Behold we left all things and followed you; what then will be to us?
pieces: Then Peter spoke up. "We have left everything behind and followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}," he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "So what will we receive?"

L.27: Then Peter answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, we have left everything and followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; what then will there be for us?"

R.27: Then Peter said to Jesus, "We left everything we had to follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. So what will we get?"

decisions.choice: we: emphatic, set against the young man who would not leave his wealth
decisions.reason: Peter speaks for the Twelve. They have done what the young man refused to do (4:20, 22; 9:9).

decisions.choice: what will there be for us: what reward will we have
decisions.reason: Peter asks about the treasure in heaven Jesus promised (19:21).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.heading: What the Twelve will receive

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὑμεῖς οἱ ἀκολουθήσαντές μοι ἐν τῇ παλιγγενεσίᾳ, ὅταν καθίσῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ, καθήσεσθε καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐπὶ δώδεκα θρόνους κρίνοντες τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: The and Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you that you the [ones] having followed me, in the regeneration, when sits the Son of the Man on throne of glory of him, will sit also you on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of the Israel.
pieces: Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you, when all things are made new and the Son of Man takes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious throne, you who have followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will also take your seats on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

L.28: And Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you that you who have followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, in the renewal [of all things], when the Son of Man sits on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne of glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

R.28: Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth, God will make the whole world new. Then the Son of Man will sit on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious throne as king. And you who have followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will also sit on twelve thrones. You will judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: the renewal: the new birth of the world in the age to come
alternatives: the new birth of a believer
decisions.reason: The word means a rebirth. Here it is the making new of all creation that the prophets promised (Isaiah 65:17; 66:22), when the Son of Man reigns.

decisions.choice: in the renewal goes with "you will sit"
alternatives: it goes with "you who have followed me"
decisions.reason: The phrase stands between the two. It most naturally says when the disciples will sit on thrones, not when they followed Jesus.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man on his throne of glory: Daniel 7:9-14
alternatives: a throne in the present age
decisions.reason: In Daniel thrones are set up and one like a son of man receives an everlasting kingdom. Matthew speaks again of the Son of Man's throne of glory in 25:31.

decisions.choice: judging: ruling over, and passing judgment on
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures to judge Israel often means to govern it, as the judges did. It may also include judgment at the end. The twelve disciples answer to the twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: God will make the whole world new
decisions.reason: Readable says what the renewal is.

decisions.choice: glorious throne
decisions.reason: "Glorious" keeps the key term in its adjective form.

records.source: καὶ πᾶς ὅστις ἀφῆκεν οἰκίας ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου, ἑκατονταπλασίονα λήμψεται καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσει.
records.gloss: And everyone who left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of the name of me, a hundredfold will receive and life eternal will inherit.
pieces: Anyone who has left behind houses, or brothers or sisters, or father or mother, or wife or children, or fields, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will be repaid a hundred times over and will receive eternal life as an inheritance.

L.29: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will receive a hundred times as much and will inherit eternal life.

R.29: Some people have left their homes, their brothers or sisters, their father or mother, their wife or children, or their land, because they follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They will get back a hundred times more than they left. And God will give them eternal life.

decisions.choice: for the sake of my name: because of me, for loyalty to me
alternatives: for the sake of a title
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. Compare 10:22, "hated by all because of my name".

decisions.choice: a hundred times as much: far more than was given up, in the family of God's people
decisions.reason: Jesus calls those who do God's will his brothers, sisters and mother (12:49-50). Mark 10:30 says the reward comes "now in this time", together with eternal life in the age to come.

decisions.choice: inherit: receive as heirs, a gift and not a wage
decisions.reason: An inheritance is given because one belongs to the family. Compare 25:34.

decisions.choice: or wife and a hundred times, the readings of the SBLGNT
alternatives: no mention of a wife, in some early manuscripts
many times, in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "or wife", and some read "many times" for "a hundred times", as in Luke 18:30. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with the reward told after the list
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the long list.

decisions.choice: God will give them eternal life
decisions.reason: Readable says who gives the inheritance.

records.source: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.
records.gloss: Many but will be first last and last first.
pieces: But many who are first now will end up last, and the last will end up first.

L.30: But many [who are] first will be last, and [the] last first.

R.30: But many people who are important now will be the least important then. And many who are the least important now will be the most important then.

decisions.choice: first and last: those who rank high or low now will change places in the kingdom
alternatives: the order in which people enter heaven
decisions.reason: Those who seem first now, like the rich, may be last; those who seem last, like the disciples who gave everything up, will be first. The same saying ends the parable that follows (20:16).

decisions.choice: but: a warning that follows the promise
alternatives: a contrast with the young man only
decisions.reason: After promising reward, Jesus warns that rank in the kingdom will not follow the ranks of this world, even among his followers.

decisions.choice: important now ... least important then
decisions.reason: Readable says what first and last mean.

decisions.choice: no closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer to Peter goes on into the parable of 20:1-16, which begins "For the kingdom of heaven is like". The speech closes at 20:16.
